library(readxl)

## GGplot over Time

### Analysis with Actual Data (evaluation turned off)

The actual data are *not* included in this repo.
That is, the folder `data/` is ignored (see [.gitignore](.gitignore))
Further, the dataset name has been altered.
Note also that evaluation is turned off (`eval=FALSE`);
the code chunks can be run manually but will not
evaluate upon **knit** of this document,
but the code chunks will still appear.

```{r eval=FALSE}
calwt <- read_xlsx("data/clean_data.xlsx")
```

simplify names

```{r eval=FALSE}
calwt <- rename(calwt,
  Date = "Date Time, GMT-07:00",
  Temp = "Temp, °F"
)
```

Summary. Always good to check data.

```{r eval=FALSE}
summary(calwt)
```

Plot over time of data with smooth curve (blue) and
warning block (red with pink fill).

```{r eval=FALSE}
ggplot(calwt) +
  aes(Date, Temp, ymin = 80, ymax = max(Temp), xmax = max(Date), xmin = min(Date)) +
  geom_rect(col = "red", fill = "pink") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_smooth(col = "blue")
```

### Simulated Data

Simulate data matching the empirical characteristics of `data/clean_data.xlsx`:

- **Date range & frequency**: 30-minute intervals across June–September 2025.
- **Multi-day & seasonal variation**: Oscillations over days and weeks reflecting weather fronts and summer peak (~60°F to ~87°F, mean ~74°F).
- **Daily diurnal variation**: 24-hour cycle with minimums in early morning (~8–9 AM) and maximums in late afternoon (~5–6 PM).
- **Autocorrelation & noise**: Smooth continuous variations using an AR(1) process with day-to-day swing variations.

```{r simulate-data}
set.seed(42)

# Match time range and 30-minute sampling interval of the original data
start_date <- as.POSIXct("2025-06-14 00:00:00")
end_date <- as.POSIXct("2025-09-27 23:30:00")
dates <- seq(from = start_date, to = end_date, by = "30 mins")
n <- length(dates)

# Temporal indicators
hours_from_start <- as.numeric(difftime(dates, start_date, units = "hours"))
days <- hours_from_start / 24
hour_of_day <- as.numeric(format(dates, "%H")) + as.numeric(format(dates, "%M")) / 60

# 1. Multi-day weather fronts and seasonal trend (mean ~74.3°F, range ~62-82°F)
baseline_trend <- 74.3 +
  3.8 * sin(2 * pi * (days - 20) / 110) + # broad summer seasonal arc
  3.2 * sin(2 * pi * days / 12) +         # ~12-day weather cycles
  1.8 * cos(2 * pi * days / 5)            # ~5-day short weather oscillations

# 2. Daily diurnal cycle (trough ~8:30 AM, peak ~5:30 PM, daily amplitude ~3.7°F)
diurnal_cycle <- 3.7 * sin(2 * pi * (hour_of_day - 13.5) / 24)

# 3. Day-to-day variation in daily range
day_index <- floor(days) + 1
amplitude_mod <- rnorm(max(day_index), mean = 1, sd = 0.2)[day_index]

# 4. Short-term autocorrelated noise (AR(1))
noise <- as.numeric(arima.sim(model = list(ar = 0.92), n = n, sd = 0.35))

# Assemble simulated data frame
sim_calwt <- data.frame(
  Date = dates,
  Temp = round(baseline_trend + (diurnal_cycle * amplitude_mod) + noise, 2)
)
```

### Analysis of Simulated Data (evaluation shown)

Summary of simulated data:

```{r sim-summary}
summary(sim_calwt)
```

Plot of simulated data with the same styling.
Plot over time of data with smooth curve (blue) and
warning block (red with pink fill).

```{r plot-sim}
ggplot(sim_calwt) +
  aes(Date, Temp, ymin = 80, ymax = max(Temp), xmax = max(Date), xmin = min(Date)) +
  geom_rect(col = "red", fill = "pink") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_smooth(col = "blue")
```
